archetypes.name: foreground-marker-audit
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces collect-agent-results.sh and launch-review.sh inside brainstorm.md fences — both Family B denylisted scripts. BASH_AUTHORING.md §4 mandates a literal banner above each fence plus a per-anchor in-fence comment within five lines of each anchor; the plan mentions this requirement but does not enumerate which exact lines satisfy it, leaving a gap that would fail make lint-foreground-markers.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/lint-foreground-markers.sh and scripts/lint-foreground-markers.md to identify the exact banner and per-anchor comment strings the linter matches. Then read the plan's proposed brainstorm.md fenced blocks and verify the plan explicitly emits each required marker in the correct position relative to every denylisted-script anchor (collect-agent-results.sh, launch-review.sh). Cross-check whether the plan's collect-agent-results.sh invocation inside brainstorm.md satisfies both the above-fence banner rule and the within-five-lines in-fence comment rule as the linter would evaluate them. Flag any fence block where the described content would fail make lint-foreground-markers or where the plan is ambiguous about marker placement. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: run-params-consumers
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds brainstorm_requested to run-params.json but only explicitly names three consumers. Any existing callsite that reconstructs or overwrites run-params.json without the new --brainstorm-requested flag would silently reset the field to false on re-entry, causing Step 1d.5 to silently skip despite --brainstorm being on the original argv.
archetypes.prompt_body: Grep scripts/ and skills/design/ for every callsite of write-run-params.sh and every jq expression that reads or writes run-params.json to build a complete consumer map. For each callsite the plan does not mention, determine whether omitting --brainstorm-requested would silently drop brainstorm_requested back to false on a gate-retry or mid-run resume, and whether the plan's proposed partition-recovery jq-merge fallback is the only recovery path or whether additional re-entry paths reconstruct run-params.json independently. Also verify that the plan's jq template change produces valid JSON when brainstorm_requested is omitted by older callers (backward-compat claim). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: never-rule-compliance
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a normatively-sanctioned anti-halt override for the brainstorm free-form loop — an unusual control-flow exception that must be precisely scoped and must not conflict with SKILL.md NEVER directives or the canonical orchestrator-never.md policy, and the plan's termination-detection vocabulary list introduces semantic ambiguity that could cause the loop to continue or terminate unexpectedly.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/design/SKILL.md's NEVER list and skills/shared/orchestrator-never.md to identify all directives that govern turn-boundary semantics, ScheduleWakeup, and anti-halt continuation. Verify that the plan's proposed anti-halt override in brainstorm.md is scoped strictly to the brainstorm loop (lifted by sentinel write) and does not create a loophole that would permit inadvertent turn-ending in other steps. Check whether the plan's termination-detection vocabulary list (ready, proceed, next, go to sketches, etc.) overlaps with phrases a user might type during normal design discussion, creating a false-termination risk, and whether the plan provides sufficient guidance for the main agent to distinguish termination signals from continued refinement. Flag any NEVER rule the proposed override language conflicts with or silently weakens. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
